chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Joining Charlie Barnet at the Park Central Hotel
summary: Barnet worked briefly, loved Duke and patterned his band on Ellington, with arrangements by Andy Gibson.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So I went with Barnet later, and Barnet, when I went with him, he was working at the Park Central Hotel in New York. They used bands upstairs there then, and we were there about two, three months, and then we went out on the road, and we did a few theaters and a few one nighters, but Barnet never would work too long. He -- I guess he had money, and he just didn't care.
He loved Duke, you know. He always tried to pattern his band after Duke's, you know, and he -- oh, we played a lot of things that Duke played, you know, not the same arrangements, but --

Andy Gibson, and he tried to copy as close as he could, but most of them were Duke's things. But Barnet always did have a good band. He would hire good men. He'd pay them well. It's ironic, but I remember Barnet -- he didn't have a lot of hit records or anything, but I made more money than I made with -- ever made with Lunceford, you know.
